name: Meleagant

attributes.attribute: a king or giant who took Queen Guinevere
his name also appears as Melwas
king of Somerset, the Land of the Summer, maybe a fairy king

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Meleagant is a figure in Arthurian legend. His name is also written Melwas, Meleagraunce, and Mellyagraunce. He was a king or a giant. He kidnapped queen Guinevere and held her. The knight Lancelot went to set her free. In one account the saint Gildas made him release her. To reach her, Lancelot crossed a strange bridge. The route ran under the water, or above it on a knife-edge. Lancelot took the upper path and cut himself badly. In her room he lay beside her, and the sheets turned red. His friend Kay waited hurt in the same room. Meleagant came on the blood and blamed Kay. Lancelot defended Kay and freed the queen. Meleagant was the king of Somerset, the Land of Summer. He may first have been a god or a fairy king.
